title: Hybrid parallel highlighting: use Hyperscan where supported, QtRegex where not, run both in parallel

summary.problem: Highlighting currently relies primarily on Qt regex evaluation and can lag/freeze when many highlight rules are enabled, especially on large logs.
summary.goal: Implement a hybrid highlighting engine: classify highlight patterns into Hyperscan-compatible vs QtRegex-only; compile Hyperscan patterns into a multi-pattern database; execute Hyperscan scan and QtRegex fallback scans in parallel across multiple cores; cache results; support both background full-file highlighting and on-demand visible-line highlighting without blocking the UI.

scope: Hybrid engine selection per pattern (Hyperscan vs QtRegex).
Parallel execution across CPU cores using thread pool / QtConcurrent / existing worker infra.
Highlight cache storage and retrieval for renderer.
Just-in-time highlighting for visible lines if not yet cached.
Maintain highlight precedence/override semantics identical to current behavior.
out_of_scope: UI/UX redesign of highlight rule editor.
New settings UI (optional debug flags ok).
Log rotation/truncation handling beyond current behavior.
assumptions: Klogg already stores/loads highlight rule sets and applies them during rendering.
Highlight precedence is order-based (later rules override earlier rules).
Hyperscan is available on supported builds/CPUs; otherwise fallback to Qt-only.
Log lines are processed independently for highlighting (no multi-line highlight semantics required).
acceptance_criteria: Patterns that compile with Hyperscan are highlighted using Hyperscan; patterns that fail Hyperscan compilation use QtRegex.
Both engines can run concurrently without blocking the UI thread.
Background highlighting uses multicore chunking and populates a cache indexed by line.
On-demand (visible line) highlighting uses hybrid matching in a worker thread and updates cache/UI asynchronously.
Qt-only mode (Hyperscan unavailable) still uses multicore parallel chunking to improve performance vs current sequential behavior.
Visual output (highlight spans and precedence) is identical to the legacy implementation for the same rule set.
No data races: thread-safe use of Hyperscan scratch space per worker and safe cache updates.
No regressions: highlighting remains correct when rules are edited, enabled/disabled, or reordered.
deliverables: Pattern classification + compilation pipeline (Hyperscan multi-compile + Qt compiled regex list).
Parallel highlight execution engine (Hyperscan scan + QtRegex scan in parallel).
Highlight cache keyed by (file-id, highlight-rule-set-version, line-number).
Renderer integration to use cache; non-blocking on-demand computation.
Instrumentation (debug logs/counters) for engine usage, timings, and cache hits.
Unit/integration tests verifying correctness and core performance properties.

implementation_plan.title: Discovery: map current highlighting pipeline and data structures
actions: Locate the highlighter/rules classes, the renderer hook that requests highlight spans, and the current regex evaluation path.
Identify where highlight rules are parsed/compiled (Qt QRegularExpression usage).
Find how line text is fetched (string encoding) and how highlight spans are represented (offset/length/style).
Find any existing caching mechanism for highlights; if none, confirm renderer recomputes on demand.
expected_output: List of key files/classes to modify, and a call-chain diagram in PR description.

implementation_plan.title: Introduce engine-aware rule representation
actions: Create a new internal struct to represent a highlight rule with metadata: id, priority/order, pattern text, options, style/color payload.
Add engine classification fields: engine = {Hyperscan, QtRegex}, compile status, error message if any.
Ensure rules are versioned by a rule-set generation id that increments on any rule change (add/remove/edit/reorder).

implementation_plan.title: Pattern compatibility check + compilation (classification stage)
actions: Attempt Hyperscan compilation for each enabled rule in a batch using hs_compile_multi.
If a rule fails compilation, classify it as QtRegex-only and compile with QRegularExpression.
Store compiled artifacts: Hyperscan database + per-thread scratch alloc template; Qt compiled regex objects.
Cache compiled artifacts keyed by (file-view id, rule-set generation id) so recompilation only happens when rules change.
notes: Prefer hs_compile_multi for all HS-compatible patterns in one database for single-pass matching.
Allocate Hyperscan scratch per worker thread (clone from a base scratch).
Compilation errors should be recorded but must not break highlighting; fallback to Qt.

implementation_plan.title: Define highlight result model and cache
actions: Define a canonical highlight span representation: {startColumn, length, styleId/ruleId}.
Create a cache structure indexed by lineNumber -> vector<Span>.
Cache must be scoped per (fileId, ruleSetGen) and invalidated on rule changes or file reload.
Cache supports partial population (some lines computed, others pending).
cache_requirements: Optional LRU behavior or memory cap is acceptable but not required for first iteration.

implementation_plan.title: Hybrid matching for a line range (core engine API)
actions: Implement a function HighlightRange(lineStart, lineEnd) that returns per-line spans for the range.
Inside HighlightRange: run Hyperscan scan for HS patterns and run QtRegex scan for Qt-only patterns in parallel.
Merge results per line, respecting rule priority (later rules override earlier rules).
Return batched results suitable for cache insertion.
parallelism_design: Option A: Two parallel tasks: (1) HS scan whole range, (2) Qt scan whole range. Merge.
Option B: Chunk the range into N segments; each segment task runs HS + Qt (or HS only + Qt only tasks) to maximize core utilization.
Start with Option B for background scanning; Option A may be sufficient for small visible ranges.

implementation_plan.title: Hyperscan scan implementation details
actions: Create HS match callback capturing: patternId(ruleId), match end offset, and (if needed) derive start offset.
Map byte offsets back to (line, column). Use a precomputed mapping for the scanned buffer: newline offsets array or per-line start offsets.
Convert source text for HS scanning to a stable encoding (typically UTF-8) and ensure column mapping accounts for encoding differences (prefer ASCII logs; otherwise define policy).
Use one hs_scan per chunk; each worker has its own scratch.
notes: If precise start offsets are not available from HS (depending on compile flags), you can compute start by re-running a minimal check on the matched line with Qt for that specific pattern, but this should be rare and optional.
If the current renderer expects character indices, ensure conversion is consistent.

implementation_plan.title: QtRegex fallback scan implementation details (parallel)
actions: Precompile QRegularExpression for each Qt-only rule.
Implement scanning per line for each regex; collect spans (start, length).
Parallelize using chunking by line range across thread pool (each task handles a block of lines and runs all Qt-only regex rules on those lines).
Avoid per-line allocations; reuse buffers and vectors.
notes: Do not spawn one thread per regex; prefer chunk-by-lines to avoid oversubscription.

QRegularExpression matching is safe to call concurrently when each thread uses its own QRegularExpression instance or uses const shared instances depending on Qt guarantees; choose the safer approach if uncertain.

implementation_plan.title: Merge and precedence resolution
actions: Define deterministic merge rules: if multiple spans overlap, the higher priority (later rule) wins for the overlapping region.
Implement span normalization: sort spans by start, apply overrides by priority, produce final non-overlapping spans per line.
Ensure this matches existing behavior exactly.

implementation_plan.title: Background full-file highlighting (pre-scan)
actions: On file load or highlight rule-set change: schedule background highlight job(s) to compute highlights for entire file.
Split file into N line-range chunks; process with HighlightRange concurrently on the worker pool.
Insert results into cache incrementally; notify UI to repaint regions as chunks complete.
Support cancelation via generation id: if rules change mid-scan, discard results.

implementation_plan.title: On-demand visible-range highlighting (just-in-time)
actions: When renderer requests highlights for a line range: serve from cache if present.
If some lines are missing: enqueue a worker job to compute those lines via HighlightRange; immediately render without highlights or with partial highlights, then repaint once results arrive.
Coalesce requests during fast scrolling (debounce) and compute a slightly larger window around viewport to reduce churn.

implementation_plan.title: Qt-only mode improvements (when Hyperscan unavailable)
actions: If Hyperscan is not available/disabled, still use the same parallel chunk-by-lines approach for Qt regex matching.
Keep the same cache + background/on-demand structure to improve responsiveness relative to sequential evaluation.

implementation_plan.title: Instrumentation and debugging hooks
actions: Add debug logs/counters: number of HS rules, Qt rules, compile failures, scan time per chunk, cache hit rate, number of spans generated.
Optional: dev flag to annotate which engine produced spans (for validation).

implementation_plan.title: Tests: correctness and performance properties
actions: Unit tests: span merge/precedence correctness (overlaps).
Unit tests: rule classification (HS compile success/failure routes to correct engine).
Integration test: compare legacy Qt-only highlighting output to hybrid output for a controlled log sample (must match).
Integration test: large rule-set performance sanity (ensure no UI-thread blocking by asserting work happens on worker threads / using timing hooks).

implementation_plan.title: Performance validation and regression guardrails
actions: Add a local benchmark script or debug command that measures highlight computation time on a sample large file with many rules.
Verify scaling with CPU cores (N threads) for background scan.
Ensure memory usage of cache is acceptable; optionally add soft cap / LRU later if needed.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Mapping Hyperscan byte offsets to line/column may be non-trivial if text encoding is UTF-16/UTF-8 mixed.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Standardize HS scanning input to UTF-8 with explicit mapping arrays (newline offsets + per-line UTF-8 to column conversion policy); or restrict HS highlighting to ASCII lines initially.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Highlight precedence might diverge from legacy behavior when merges are done concurrently.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Centralize merge logic in one deterministic function and validate against legacy output with tests.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Thread contention or too many jobs causing overhead.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Use chunk-by-lines with bounded thread pool; coalesce visible-range requests; avoid per-regex threads.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Hyperscan compile failures for many patterns could cause slow Qt path only.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Keep classification cached; provide debug visibility into which rules are HS vs Qt and why.

definition_of_done: Hybrid highlighting engine is implemented and enabled by default when Hyperscan is available.
Qt-only mode uses multicore chunking and the same cache pipeline.
No UI blocking during scrolling; highlighting arrives asynchronously and is cached.
Tests pass and output matches legacy highlighting semantics.

guidance: Prefer minimal invasive refactor: wrap existing highlighter rule evaluation behind a new hybrid engine facade and reuse existing renderer/span structures.
Do not change rule editor UI; keep rule semantics identical.
Keep code modular so future work can add Hyperscan support for more constructs or integrate with search engine improvements.
